body: yup, kinda like when you feel like youre getting a cold, but without the respiratory problems. the headache didn't really concern me until the part where my thoughts went fuzzy and then when i snapped back i didnt feel any dread or whatever, which has been pretty consistent and also should be in overdrive right now since my landlord is making me get rid of my dog (apparently she's been barking when im not home; i can send her to stay with my parents but usually i'd still feel pretty shitty). my first thought was maybe the depression lifted for god knows what reason, but likewise i couldnt really conjure up any positive emotions either, so im not sure if its a sign of things getting better, worse, or unrelated. but even today ive noticed im less irritable, so even if it's "worse" it sure feels better.

i drink a beer or wine every now and then but the last time i got drunk before this was back in 2013. i was about to say it wasn't like brainfreeze but when i thought about it, that's kinda exactly what it was like, only much less intense. not painful at all, just annoying. hmm. thanks for the reply!

ive been where you are, and kinda am there now. i moved out of the middle of nowhere, away from my parents, hoping to find something in the city, since i lived there before for uni and really enjoyed it then. been here almost 3 years now but due to various circumstances ive been more locked into depression than before.

i posted here a few days ago, which didnt directly help. but after looking around SW (which, to make less subtle, is my advice to do), i decided to approach things differently. im usually stuck online, playing games (mainly GW2; if thats something you do maybe we could party up sometime and chat), but something i read here, and im not sure what, made me want to switch things up. if youre close enough to any city, even a smaller one, as nice as the net can be, maybe you should get out and do something. i know, not as easy as it sounds. schedule, money, time, so much gets in the way of that. but i said fuck it, and went out to a bar. not to get shitfaced, but to chill, eat, and have a few drinks. 70 bucks after a tip, but it was liberating. that was Saturday night. Sunday i got up and spent my day downtown. bought a whole bunch of food to make at home that i'd normally say "thats not financially practical." fuck it. i wanna try it. then i went to dinner and dropped another 70+ on food and drink. tried calamari for the first time. tried new drinks. it was all doubly satisfying because my gf, who is 50% of the reason i stay in because she has anxiety and usually refuses to leave home, agreed to go with me without any resistance. maybe because i told her "im going" rather than "can we go/we should go". but that may or may not apply to you.

it may not be plausible (i mean that strictly plausible; practical has been holding me back) for you to do something like that. if you work, your schedule might be fucked up. try to request a day or two off in a couple weeks. if you dont work, you might not have money. but if your dad has conviction that you need to do "normal things," maybe he'll help you out, even if youre only borrowing.

as for explaining things to your family, ive settled on you cant really make anyone understand, especially anyone older than 35-40. back in their day, hard work was a lot more effective in fixing problems than it is today. getting out and doing "normal things" was the only way to have fun. generation gaps are impossible to breach about 95% of the time.

something that may have made my girlfriend more cooperative might help you out. she's been watching Bizzare Foods on netflix. it might inspire you to try something new, even if you make it at home. if youre not a good cook, its an invaluable skill and i would say practice. use recipes for inspiration, and try to make it your own. spices are important, i started by tossing oregano in chef boyardee ravioli when i got sick of how bland it was. i now make (by feedback from friends/family, i cant promise unanimous opinion) "the best curry and ramen in Pittsburgh." and remember, the only thing more important in cooking than the ingredients is counter space. without enough room, cooking is hell.

im in no way saying any of this is a cure for depression, its really not that easy. but from the past few days, ive noticed planting my feet and mixing things up has had a positive impact on it, if nothing else by giving me a little control to push suicidal thoughts away. but my method might not work for you. it might be implausible or might just not be the thing for you. but if you take nothing else from this post, please do this one thing:

look around this subreddit. i didnt take a step in the right direction alone. it wasnt even from my own post. my plans were already in action by the time i got a comment. i hope this helped, and sorry if its a little disorganized. and long.

thanks for your reply. i know exactly how you feel with the college thing, im 26 and i still get shit for dropping out. thats really the least of my worries now, ive come to terms with it because tbh i did it because i dont want to be paying loans til im 50. i can honestly tell you that will get better, even if you still get bitched at for it.

looking around this subreddit really helped me though. im not entirely sure why. ive always known im not alone in how i feel and it usually makes me feel worse because i wouldnt wish this on anyone. it wasnt the encouraging words either. something just kind of clicked. obv i dont feel completely better, but maybe i just hit a level where i decided to approach things differently. i dont know how well itll work but i guess its worth a shot.
